note: Whether a SessionStart command hook that prints hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext reaches the session's context, what an empty print does, and the size, timing and trust limits on that path. Field names, type names, counts, timings and verdicts only; no prompt, reply, probe word, id or path is recorded.

registration: one SessionStart command hook passed with --settings, matcher empty, --setting-sources project in an empty scratch folder so no user settings or plugins added hooks
recorder: a probe script that saved its stdin to the scratch folder and printed the ruled JSON with a random probe word in additionalContext, or nothing
zero_cost_method: an unrecognised --model name: the SessionStart hook runs and the transcript and debug log record what it injected, then the session stops before any model request
credential: the account's own sign-in; nothing was read or copied

note: No model or permission_mode key, unlike Codex.

verdict: ACCEPTED: the debug log reports the hook provided additionalContext and gives its length in chars.

what: ruled JSON, about 40 chars, one probe word
verdict: REACHED: the model named the probe word from the injected text.
ADDS NOTHING: no hook_success and no hook_additional_context record is written, and the model saw no probe word.

what: ruled JSON, 12,000 chars, one probe word at the head and one at the tail
verdict: OVER THE LIMIT IS NOT TRUNCATED IN PLACE: the whole output is saved to a file under the session's tool-results folder and the context gets a persisted-output block holding the file path and a 2 KB preview, so only the head reaches the model.

unit: characters, not bytes: 6,000 two-byte characters (12,000 bytes) stayed inline
verdict: additionalContext up to 10,000 characters is injected whole; 10,001 or more is replaced by the saved-file preview.

what: ruled JSON after an 8 s sleep, no timeout set
verdict: WAITED FOR: the first model request starts only after the hook finishes, so a slow hook delays the session by its own duration and its text still arrives.

what: ruled JSON after a 5 s sleep, hook timeout set to 2
verdict: KILLED AT THE TIMEOUT: the hook is cancelled, nothing is injected, and the session carries on.

order: both before the person's first user record
verdict: The injected text is stored in the transcript twice: once as the hook_success stdout (the whole printed JSON) and once as the hook_additional_context content.

measured: headless -p only, where the workspace trust dialog does not run
verdict: No trust prompt in this path. Interactive trust and plugin-registered hooks were not measured here.

items: the default hook timeout when none is set (only that 8 s was waited for in full)
interactive sessions, source values other than startup
a plugin-registered hook rather than one from --settings
